experiments.title: Learning when historical context worsens attack-stage decisions
experiments.finding: Higher movement recall than ordinary gating, with more false alerts and higher weighted error in all five conditions

experiments.title: Selecting stage evidence under availability and deadline constraints
experiments.finding: Lower simulated spend but no robust detection advantage; some better F1 comparisons suppress attack warnings

experiments.title: Measuring time-split sensitivity in attack-stage classification
experiments.finding: Time-mixed training raises macro-F1 by .0632/.0383 on identical anchor rows; diagnostic, not deployment improvement

experiments.title: Transferring a context-selection score policy between recent security datasets
experiments.finding: Cost-sensitive hard decisions match context in all 42 views; no added decision benefit. Secondary T1105 policy transfer, not movement/exfiltration confirmation

experiments.title: Temporal validity and warning retention in APT-stage benchmarking
experiments.finding: DAPT cannot support an all-native-class single chronological cutoff; SCVIC has possible recorded-start support but unqualified physical clocks; DSRL is DAPT-derived synthetic data; S-DAPT has no qualified acquired release. Portable planner reproduces PX-082 exactly.

experiments.title: Calibrating stage-conditioned missed-warning risk
experiments.finding: Stage calibration did not repair the primary exfiltration misses; movement absent from calibration; no deployment guarantee.

experiments.title: Recoverability decomposition and seed-ensemble stability
experiments.finding: Mean ensemble erased warnings; roles-state warning union reached 98.78% exfiltration warning recall with 196 benign false alerts.

experiments.title: Cost-ordered acquisition and warning-aware stopping
experiments.finding: 90% attack-confidence stopping saved 7.09% simulated roles acquisition cost in clean budget 2, preserving warning recalls and false-alert count; slight stage-F1 decrease.

experiments.title: Selective risk control under analyst capacity
Hard constraints for a binary warning model

inference_rule: These are exposed-data development studies. Freeze source and protocol before fitting; keep all registered outcomes. Do not infer independent-campaign efficacy, novelty, or a guarantee from a good score.

completed_manuscript.title: When Better APT Scores Hide Missed Attack Warnings
completed_manuscript.scope: Existing completed models, 36-pair retrospective reanalysis and independent source qualification; zero new fits
completed_manuscript.generalization_limit: One exposed campaign; four-source qualification is not four-source fitted replication
